uuid_notes.weather_request_service: A random 128-bit base of its own (WX3 #1188), deliberately NOT a block inside the OBC Control base: iOS matches the advertisement on this UUID alone, so the two services must be independently advertisable. Both live in GATT at all times — the device swaps which one it ADVERTISES. Advertising byte order is the display form reversed: AA B5 54 4D 95 E5 FF A5 02 4F B4 33 00 00 B6 B3
uuid_notes.weather_request_context: The read-only, authenticated request-context characteristic. Authenticated because the value says where the rider is; an unbonded peer gets an ATT security error and does not consume the pending request

feature_bits._note: The protocolVersion read's trailing feature_bits u32 (spec 1, WX3 #1188). One bit covers the whole Weather Request contract — the secondary service, the request context, object type 20 and the Config refresh field — because a phone that has only some of those can do nothing. Unknown bits are ignored; an absent word means a firmware that predates it, never a fabricated 0

half a posting below the cell seam — the upper corners come from the next cell (di 31.5, dj 3)
half a posting past the east coverage edge — clamped to the last covered sample, not extrapolated to 424

track-export.gpx.creator: OpenBikeComputer
track-export.gpx.note: the partial trailing record contributes no <trkpt>; hr/cad/pwr = 0 are values, not the absent sentinels

ride-v2.bin.format: ride object v2 (spec 7.2, epic #707) — BLE-sensor summary + per-point sensor fields; device may serve v1 or v2, the app must accept both
ride-v2.bin.name: Sensor Ride

config-v1.bin.name: OBC Tourer
config-v1.bin._note: No trailing refresh byte — what an app predating WX3 (#1188) writes to rename the device. A reader must take the absent field as UNSPECIFIED (device default), never as Off, or a rename silently switches weather off

config-weather-refresh.bin.format: Config (spec 7.3) with the WX3 (#1188) trailing field — name_len u16 · name · units u8 · weather_refresh u8
config-weather-refresh.bin.name: OBC Alpine
config-weather-refresh.bin._note: The pair with config-v1.bin is the fixture: same object, one appended byte. The only way to get this wrong is the offset, and an off-by-one reads the shorter file correctly. Units are imperial on purpose, so the refresh byte follows a NONZERO units byte rather than a zero a misaligned reader could take for padding. Refresh enum: 0 Off · 1 15 min · 2 30 min (default) · 3 60 min · 4 120 min; an out-of-range value is malformed, not a default

config-weather-refresh-unknown.bin.format: Config (spec 7.3) with a WX3 trailing field naming an interval no version defines
config-weather-refresh-unknown.bin.name: OBC Horizon
config-weather-refresh-unknown.bin._note: The SAME blob read twice, with two right answers (spec 11.8, #1214). Phone -> device, as a Config WRITE: rejected — a device cannot honour an interval it does not know, and storing the default, Off, or the previous value would all tell the rider their choice was applied when it was discarded. Device -> phone, as a Config READ: unknown, never fatal — an unrecognised value arriving FROM a device is a NEWER device, and a direction-blind reject would mean appending a fifth interval broke every shipped app, right down to renaming the device. Unknown is its own state: not Off, not the default, and distinguishable from ABSENT, so implementations keep the raw byte and round-trip it verbatim. Units are metric on purpose: an off-by-one reader lands on that zero and decodes a perfectly KNOWN Off, so the misalignment surfaces as a wrong answer instead of another 'unknown' the tolerant path would have accepted anyway. The 11-byte name is a third distinct length across the three Config fixtures, so no reader passes all of them with one hard-coded index

transfer-set-shard.bin.note: RETIRED by OBCM v14 (#1420): a map is one object, OBCA §5 is superseded, and this fixture is DELETED WITH THE SET MACHINERY IN FS7.5b/c rather than regenerated. mapShard: object_id is NOT an object id — it is (shard_count << 8) | index, so 0x0802 is shard 2 of 8 (OBCA 5.1). The count rides every shard, not just the first, so a device refuses an over-large set at shard 0

transfer-set-terrain.bin.note: RETIRED by OBCM v14 (#1420): the raster now lives inside the map file (OBCM §1.3), so this transfer no longer exists; DELETED IN FS7.5b/c rather than regenerated. terrainShard: the set's OBCT raster, MS<id>.OBD (OBCA 5.1's terrain role). New-only like the manifest — at most one per set, so there is nothing for an id to select. total_len/crc32 are terrain-shard.obcd's own, and it is sent after every mapShard and before the mapSet

transfer-set-manifest.bin.note: RETIRED by OBCM v14 (#1420): there is no set and no manifest; DELETED IN FS7.5b/c together with obc-formats/src/obcs.rs rather than regenerated. mapSet: the OBCS manifest, new-only and written last (OBCA 5.4). total_len is fixed by the RECORD count, not the shard count: 72 + 64 x 9 = the eight OBCM shards plus the terrain record, because OBCA 5.2's Shard Count counts every record (#1044). The record width is 64 since manifest v3 (#1389) gave every record its member ObjectId

update-container-v1.bin.format: OBCU update container (spec 1), unsigned/v1 — fwImage payload (spec 7.6)

update-container-v2.bin.format: OBCU update container (spec 1), Ed25519-signed/v2 — same header table and same 128-byte image as v1, with the scheme marker in v1's reserved bytes 48..52 and a 64-byte signature trailer
update-container-v2.bin.signed_message: sig_context (11 B, trailing NUL) || fw_version[32] || image_len u32 LE || image[image_len]

route-list.bin.format: routeList object (spec 7.4) — 6-byte v2 header + 84-byte entries (76-byte v2 core + auto-expiry tail: expires_at u32 · retention u8 · reserved u8[3], epic #638 S4)

version-read.bin.format: protocolVersion read (spec 1) — version u16 · store_epoch u32 · obcm_version u8
version-read.bin._note: obcm_version is the OBCM map-format version the reader reads (obc_formats::obcm::VERSION), NOT the protocol version beside it. The builder self-sources it, so an OBCM bump re-cuts this fixture and this number on purpose — and one is pending: OBCM_Spec.md is v14 since #1420, obc_formats::obcm::VERSION follows in FS7.5b, and this file REGENERATES WITH FS7.5b as obcm_version 14. The 13 here is correct for the constant as it stands Since WX3 (#1188) this is the read a device WITHOUT the weather contract serves — the capability word is absent, so has_weather is false; version-read-features.bin is the widened form.

version-read-features.bin.format: protocolVersion read (spec 1), WX3 #1188 — version u16 · store_epoch u32 · obcm_version u8 · feature_bits u32
version-read-features.bin._note: The only read that entitles a phone to look for the Weather Request service. The capability word is an APPEND — the protocol version underneath it does not move — and the epoch deliberately differs from the 0xA1B2C3D4 the three older identity reads share, so a consumer that opens the wrong file fails on the epoch rather than passing everything except the feature word. obcm_version is self-sourced like its siblings', and REGENERATES WITH FS7.5b as 14 (OBCM v14, #1420). A read of 8, 9 or 10 bytes is a broken u32, not a smaller capability set: it decodes as feature_bits absent.

version-read-noobcm.bin.format: protocolVersion read (spec 1), pre-#911 — version u16 · store_epoch u32
version-read-noobcm.bin._note: A firmware that predates the obcm_version byte. Decoders take the absent field as unknown (null/nil/None), never as 0 — obcm_version 0 would read as 'supports OBCM v0' and refuse every real map.

version-read-nostore.bin.format: protocolVersion read (spec 1), no mounted store — version u16 only
version-read-nostore.bin._note: No card ⇒ no era to name, and the fields are positional, so there is no room for the obcm byte after an epoch that is not there. A reader must fail its ack closed rather than read epoch 0, which is a legal era.

status-download-announce.bin.format: status msg 4 downloadAnnounce (spec 4.3) — msg byte + 12-byte descriptor

trip-v1.bin.format: trip object v1 (spec 7.7) — 56-byte header + 2 bytes/stage, references route ids
trip-v1.bin.name: Alpen Traverse

trip-list.bin.format: tripList object (spec 7.4) — 6-byte v2 header + 76-byte entries (mirrors routeList's v2 core; no expiry tail)

weather-request-context-full.bin.format: weatherRequestContext v1 (spec 11, WX3 #1188) — 52 bytes LE: version u8 · encoded_len u8 · validity u16 · reason u16 · refresh u8 · reserved0 u8 · request_id u32 · lat_udeg i32 · lon_udeg i32 · fix_utc i64 · bearing_deg u16 · speed_deci_ms u16 · route_id u16 · reserved1 u16 · bundle_generation u32 · bundle_generated_at i64 · bundle_crc32 u32
weather-request-context-full.bin._note: A rider mid-ride with everything the device can know. The bundle group identifies a bundle that EXISTS: generation and generated_at are read out of weather-dwd-96x96-9f.obcw's header and bundle_crc32 is that file's whole-object CRC-32 — the number an upload of it announced, not its internal header CRC (0xFBFBD2D2). fix_utc is exactly one 30-minute refresh interval past bundle_generated_at, so REASON_SCHEDULED is arithmetic the same file supports. route_id 7 is the waypoint route route-list.bin catalogs. Validity bits: 0 position · 1 bearing · 2 speed · 3 bundle · 4 route. Reason bits: 0 scheduled · 1 urgent · 2 retry · 3 no_bundle · 4 out_of_area. Reserved bytes are written zero but IGNORED on read, and unknown validity/reason bits are ignored rather than rejected

weather-request-context-empty.bin._note: What the GATT attribute holds between requests, so a peer that reads it out of turn gets a structurally valid 'nothing is due' rather than the last ride's coordinates. Not all-zeroes: version 1 and the default 30-minute refresh are still stated, because an all-zero attribute would decode as layout version 0 with weather switched Off, and neither is true. Every field after the refresh byte is zero

weather-request-context-no-fix.bin.format: weatherRequestContext v1 (spec 11) — an urgent request with no fix and no bundle
weather-request-context-no-fix.bin._note: Cold start indoors: the rider opened Weather before the receiver has a fix and with nothing usable on the card. This remains a well-formed diagnostics/retry request, but the current companion returns noPosition until the device supplies a fix. Two things are pinned here: absence is a CLEARED FLAG, so the zero coordinates must not put a rider at 0N 0E holding generation 0; and refresh Off configures the SCHEDULE, not the right to ask.

weather-request-context-unknown-refresh..format: weatherRequestContext v1 (spec 11) — a refresh byte this layout version does not define
weather-request-context-unknown-refresh.._note: The day a firmware appends a fifth refresh interval, this is the byte every phone already in the field receives (spec 11.8, #1214). A device -> phone read may NEVER treat it as fatal: an unrecognised value here is a newer firmware, not a malformed one, exactly as an unrecognised reason bit is. A direction-blind reject — the trap an adversarial review of PR #1214 found in the canonical Rust — would have turned an ordinary enum append into the day weather went dead on every shipped app. Readers decode it as UNKNOWN (not Off, not the default, either of which would misreport the rider's own setting) and carry the RAW byte so it round-trips verbatim. The file is weather-request-context-full.bin at every offset but two — the refresh byte at 6 and the request-id nonce at 8..12 — so the rule is checkable by byte comparison: an unknown interval costs a reader the schedule and nothing else, not the fix, the route or the bundle identity. 9 is well clear of the enum's 0..=4, so no plausible future append quietly makes this file legal

weather-request-context-southern.bin.format: weatherRequestContext v1 (spec 11) — sign coverage for the four signed fields
weather-request-context-southern.bin._note: Shaped for COVERAGE, NOT PLAUSIBILITY, like track-log.obct: no other fixture in the set carries a negative coordinate or a pre-1970 time, so until this file existed a mirror could read lat_udeg/lon_udeg as u32 and both timestamps as u64 and pass the whole suite. El Chalten, Patagonia — southern AND western hemisphere. Read unsigned, lat_udeg becomes 4245636407 (~4245N) and lon_udeg 4222081175; fix_utc (1938-04-24T22:13:20Z) and bundle_generated_at become ~1.8e19 seconds, a device whose clock is 585 billion years ahead. Visibly impossible rather than subtly wrong, which is what a sign fixture is for, and the two i64s sit at different offsets (20 and 40) so one correct sign extension cannot cover for the other. The bundle group runs the trap the other way: generation and crc32 both have their top bit set, so a mirror reading them SIGNED gets -2 and -2147483647 — a codec that 'fixed' signedness by flipping every field fails just as loudly. That group is synthetic (no checked-in OBCW has a pre-1970 generated_at), unlike the full context's, which names a real file. route_id is the one cleared group, so the file says something about a clear flag as well as the four it exercises. fix_utc is one 60-minute interval past bundle_generated_at, matching the refresh it reports

provenance.semantic_seed: WXR4 issue #1243; the production CANONICAL lattice (36,000 x 18,000 at 0.01 deg, 6 x 4 shards of 6,144 x 4,608) at an invented generation 20260810T1430Z. Object lengths and CRCs are deterministic placeholders, not a recording of a live bake: this fixture pins the document contract, and the .obcg vectors pin the bytes.
provenance.shape: obc_wx_bake::manifest_v2::Manifest exactly; the normative schema is host/obc-wx-bake/schema/manifest-v2.schema.json
provenance.deliberate_holes: f0 omits shards (2,0) and (3,0), f120 omits (5,3), so the present/dry/out-of-domain trichotomy is exercised rather than assumed; f0 shard (3,2) is the only observed one
provenance.rust_writer_check: host/obc-wx-bake manifest_v2::tests::the_shared_cross_language_fixture_is_a_document_this_baker_would_write (parsed through the deny_unknown_fields writer model)
provenance.contract: both clients parse this document and MUST derive the same shard key set from the same bbox; a listed-but-missing shard is an error, a bitmap-absent shard is dry, a shard off the grid is out of domain
provenance.shard_addressing: shards are (col, row) from the lattice's south-west corner; col is west-to-east, row is south-to-north, and a shard set is always ascending by (row, col)
provenance.longitude_convention: microdegrees in -180..180 / -90..90. west > east means the window crosses the antimeridian; any other spelling (0..360, |lon| > 180, |lat| > 90) is an error, never a clamp or a reinterpretation. OBCG_Spec.md 10.2 is normative
provenance.outcomes: covered = fetch/dry describe it; uncovered = on the lattice but outside covered_rows; out_of_domain = off the lattice or a bbox this client refuses. Only 'covered' with an empty fetch list means no rain
provenance.swift_consumer: companion-ios/Packages/OBCKit/Tests/OBCWeatherTests/ManifestV2Tests.swift (WXR5 #1244). It decodes bbox_equivalence out of THIS file and answers every case, exactly as host/obc-wx-client/tests/manifest_v2.rs does, so a case added for one language is a case the other must answer identically. The cross-language claim is now a fact rather than a plan: this is the first manifest both clients are pinned to

rejection_equivalence.why: bbox_equivalence pins the happy path; this pins the other half, which is where two JSON stacks actually rot apart. Round 1 of #1271's review ran 28 hostile documents through both readers: they disagreed on five and hard-crashed on three. Every case below is a mutation of wx-manifest-v2.json that BOTH clients must answer identically, and none of them may crash, trap or panic — a manifest is the one document every rider fetches first, from a network. Round 2 added the integral-float family: the corpus pinned the NON-integral spelling of every number and the integral one at /version alone, so integral floats in every other field were the untested middle, and six of them diverged.
rejection_equivalence.apply: Each case patches a fresh copy of wx-manifest-v2.json. A patch is an ordered list of {op, path, value}: op 'set' assigns value at the JSON Pointer path (creating a top-level key if absent), op 'remove' deletes the member or array element. Paths are RFC 6901 with no escapes needed.
rejection_equivalence.verdicts: 'rejected' = the parser refuses the whole document (which error it names is each language's business). 'accepted' = the document parses; 'skipped_frames' is how many frame entries the lenient half then refused, and defaults to 0. The document/entry strictness split is stated in both module docs; these cases pin the type coercions underneath it, which is what the docs could not say.

cases.name: version-is-a-float
cases.why: 2.0 is not 2. Swift's JSONDecoder folds an integral Double into Int and used to accept it; serde does not

cases.name: version-is-a-string
cases.why: the document's identity is a number

cases.name: version-is-a-later-one
cases.why: an unknown version is a hard stop; guessing at a format is not an option

cases.name: previous-generations-is-null
cases.why: an explicit null is a statement, and it is not a list. Swift's decodeIfPresent used to read it as absent

cases.name: previous-generations-is-absent
cases.why: …while a genuinely missing key is the first generation ever published

cases.name: previous-generations-past-the-retention-cap
cases.why: OBCG 10.4 caps the chain at two; a longer one means the client and the sweep disagree about which generations exist

cases.name: previous-generation-is-a-path-segment
cases.why: a generation is joined into a URL

cases.name: reference-time-is-missing
cases.why: a required member

cases.name: validity-uses-a-space-separator
cases.why: RFC 3339 5.6 permits an application to accept a space and chrono does; Swift's ISO-8601 parser does not. The strict reading wins: the baker writes T

cases.name: validity-carries-a-zone-offset
cases.why: a legal RFC 3339 instant, and the same instant

cases.name: validity-carries-fractional-seconds
cases.why: legal, and truncated to the second by both

cases.name: lattice-is-larger-than-the-planet
cases.why: CRASHER. width straight off the wire, unbounded: (width + shard_width - 1) traps in Swift and shard_cols * shard_rows overflows in Rust

cases.name: shard-grid-overflows-its-own-count
cases.why: CRASHER. shard_cols * shard_rows and the bitmap's (count + 7) / 8 both overflow

cases.name: shard-grid-does-not-tile-the-lattice
cases.why: the client's arithmetic and the baker's would disagree about which object holds a cell

cases.name: covered-rows-past-the-lattice
cases.why: not a range of this grid

cases.name: key-prefix-has-an-empty-segment
cases.why: the prefix is joined onto the service origin

cases.name: cadence-disagrees-with-the-frame-list
cases.why: a mis-derived cycle, caught cheaply

cases.name: stale-after-is-before-the-next-generation
cases.why: the generation would expire before its own replacement is due

cases.name: manifest-max-age-is-negative
cases.why: clamped to zero rather than refused: it only makes the client refetch sooner

cases.name: presence-is-not-hex-at-all
cases.why: CRASHER. 'aäb' is four bytes, so a byte-sliced hex parse cuts a character in half and Rust panicked

cases.name: presence-has-an-odd-digit-count
cases.why: half a byte is not a byte

cases.name: presence-and-the-shard-list-disagree
cases.why: two spellings of one fact. Refused rather than reconciled: either direction invents whether an object exists

cases.name: crc-carries-a-sign
cases.why: from_str_radix and Swift's hex parse both used to accept '+'. A CRC is hex digits

cases.name: crc-prefix-is-uppercase
cases.why: the document's own spelling is 0x; 0X is a different string and this reader does not normalise it

cases.name: shard-claims-zero-bytes
cases.why: an object that exists has a length

cases.name: shard-is-off-the-grid
cases.why: a shard the bitmap has no bit for

cases.name: an-unknown-top-level-field
cases.why: additive fields are how the baker ships; refusing them would make every deploy an outage

cases.name: attribution-is-absent
cases.why: tolerated, because a missing credit is not a reason to lose the weather

cases.name: two-entries-name-one-shard
cases.why: the second entry is rewritten to name the first one's shard, so the bitmap claims one more shard than the list distinctly names. Duplicate entries are where a sort's stability decides which bytes and which CRC a rider fetches, so both clients pin the same answer rather than the same luck

cases.name: presence-hex-carries-a-sign
cases.why: FD1. `UInt8(_:radix:)` and `from_str_radix` both accept a leading '+', so '+0+0+0' parsed as a valid all-zero bitmap on one side and was refused on the other. Hex digits are hex digits; the shard list is emptied so the frame is otherwise well formed and only the sign decides

cases.name: presence-hex-without-a-sign-is-the-control
cases.why: the same document with plain zeros: accepted by both, so the case above is about the sign and not about the empty shard list

cases.name: cadence-frames-is-an-integral-float
cases.why: FD2, document level. 9.0 is not 9, and the count of frames is not a measurement

cases.name: lattice-width-is-an-integral-float
cases.why: FD2, document level. A cell count is an integer; a lattice cannot be 36000.0 cells wide

cases.name: manifest-max-age-is-an-integral-float
cases.why: FD2, document level. Seconds are whole here — the non-integral spelling was already pinned, and the integral one was the untested middle

cases.name: shard-bytes-is-an-integral-float
cases.why: FD2, entry level. An object length is a count of bytes, so the entry is refused and the frame with it — lenient, not fatal

cases.name: frame-offset-is-an-integral-float
cases.why: FD2, entry level, on the field that names the object. Same answer for the exponent spelling, which is why the rule is about the number's type and not about how it was written

cases.name: an-unknown-field-may-be-a-float
cases.why: the counterweight to FD2, and the reason the rule is not 'no float anywhere in the document': a reader ignores fields it does not know, so a float in one must not fail the parse. A blanket refusal would be a fresh divergence in the opposite direction

resample_equivalence.why: WXR5 #1244's uniform east-west resample, pinned across the two clients by its OUTPUT rather than by its arithmetic. Byte counts alone are not enough: at the raw4 worst case every tile is 128 bytes whatever is in it, so a half-cell drift in the nearest-neighbour column map moves which cells a rider sees while every length and every budget still passes. So each row pins the decoded cell image too.
resample_equivalence.scenario: For each latitude: corridor = a 90,000 m disc around (lat, 7.9 E) built by the shared Bbox::around/aroundCoordinate rule; lattice = the canonical one in this fixture's `lattice` block; nine frames at valid_from + i*900 for i in 0..8; each frame is one crop covering the whole lattice-aligned corridor window whose cell (row-major, row 0 = south) at flat index n is ((n * 7 + i) % 13), i.e. deliberately incompressible so every tile encodes raw4; frame i is observed iff i == 0; the hourly half is tests/fixtures/met-freiburg-24h.json decoded at offset 0.
resample_equivalence.cells_hash: FNV-1a 64 over frame 0's decoded cells as read back through the device's own OBCW reader, row-major, row 0 = south, one byte per cell: h = 0xcbf29ce484222325; for each byte b: h ^= b; h = (h * 0x100000001b3) mod 2^64. Written as 16 lowercase hex digits.
resample_equivalence.guard: Both suites also assert the two-sided guard the mechanism was chosen for: bundle_bytes <= 204800, and the output cells square to within 2 % (east-west pitch against the lattice's own 1,113 m north-south pitch).
